job.title: 462. Integrity Staffing- Medical Receptionist

About the Opportunity
We are seeking an experienced and organised Medical Receptionist to join our client, based at Sir Charles Gairdner Hospital in Nedlands.
This is a fantastic opportunity for a confident medical administration professional to provide front-line reception and administrative support within a busy clinical environment.
Working clinic hours of 7:30am – 3:30pm, you will play an important role in supporting patient services, coordinating appointments and referrals, and ensuring the smooth day-to-day operation of the unit.
This is an initial 6-month contract, with the potential for extension. An immediate start is preferred to support upcoming annual and maternity leave.
Key Responsibilities
  • Provide professional and welcoming front-line reception, greeting patients, carers and visitors.
  • Manage incoming phone calls, email enquiries and general patient correspondence.
  • Coordinate patient appointments, scheduling and diary management.
  • Assist with patient check-in, patient flow and appointment reminders, including SMS communications.
  • Support referral processing, tracking and coordination.
  • Maintain accurate patient records, scheduling trackers and administrative documentation.
  • Liaise with clinicians, internal teams and external referral sources.
  • Monitor appointment schedules, identify booking conflicts and escalate issues where required.
  • Ensure all administrative activities comply with privacy, confidentiality and relevant procedures.
  • Provide flexible administrative support across reception, scheduling and referral coordination.
About You
To be successful in this role, you will have:
  • Previous Medical Receptionist experience – essential.
  • Demonstrated appointment scheduling and diary management experience – essential.
  • Experience working in a busy medical, healthcare or clinical environment.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with a professional and approachable manner.
  • Strong organisational skills and exceptional attention to detail.
  • The ability to manage competing priorities and work efficiently in a fast-paced environment.
  • Confidence using medical administration systems, managing patient records and coordinating referrals.
  • A strong understanding of patient confidentiality and privacy requirements.
  • The ability to work both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.
What's on Offer?
  • Competitive hourly rate of $40 per hour + superannuation.
  • 37.5 hours per week.
  • Consistent clinic hours of 7:30am – 3:30pm.
  • Convenient location at Sir Charles Gairdner Hospital, Nedlands.
  • Initial 6-month with potential for extension.
  • Opportunity to contribute to an important clinical service within the Cancer Trials Unit.
  • Immediate start available.
How to Apply
If you have strong medical reception and scheduling experience and are available to commence ASAP, we would love to hear from you!

Do you have any leave booked over this time?

job.description:
We are currently seeking Camera Operators for multiple opportunities across Western Australia.

This is a hands-on, operational role responsible for the deployment and operation of mobile traffic camera equipment, contributing to road safety across WA. You’ll work independently across allocated locations, setting up and monitoring camera equipment, completing operational records and ensuring equipment is operated safely and accurately.

The assignment will run until 30/06/2027

Current vacancies
  • Neerabup
  • Mandurah
  • Geraldton
  • Midland

The role
As a Camera Operator, your duties will include:
  • Travelling to allocated camera locations and setting up, repositioning and operating mobile camera equipment
  • Monitoring and checking camera equipment to ensure it is operating accurately
  • Undertaking preliminary fault diagnosis and reporting equipment issues
  • Recording operational and location information and maintaining accurate documentation
  • Ensuring camera equipment, vehicles and associated equipment remain safe and secure
  • Communicating professionally with members of the public when required
  • Driving independently to camera sites across metropolitan and/or regional locations
  • Preparing operational reports and documentation, including information that may be required for court proceedings.


Hours & roster
These positions are 75 hours per fortnight, working a rotating three-week roster.
The standard rotation consists of:
  • 8 afternoon shifts
  • 2 days off
  • 7 day shifts
  • 4 days off

Standard shifts are 7.5 hours

Typical shift times include:
  • Day shift: 7:00am – 2:30pm
  • Afternoon shift: 2:30pm – 10:00pm
  • School zone day shift: 6:00am – 1:30pm
  • School zone afternoon shift: 1:00pm – 8:30pm


There are also opportunities for voluntary overtime in addition to standard rostered hours. This may be approximately 3 additional hours per day, up to a maximum of 5 days per swing.

About you
To be considered, you will need:
  • A current Western Australian C or CA Class Driver’s Licence
  • The physical capacity to lift and move bulky camera equipment
  • Good communication skills and the confidence to interact with members of the public, including managing difficult situations professionally
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to undertake basic equipment fault diagnosis
  • Good attention to detail and the ability to maintain accurate operational records
  • The ability to work independently and safely across different locations
  • Flexibility to work a rotating roster
  • National Police Clearance
